o1.biggest_strength: Clean, correct, evidence-led plan with a simple weekly rhythm and drafts that use real customer phrases ('replaying today's emails', 'stopped by day three') in a warm voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: Drafts drift slightly toward instruction ('Breathe out, slow and long', 'Feel your hands') and some on-screen lines read more like cues than invitations, which weakens the 'invite, don't instruct' principle.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten each draft so every on-screen line is an invitation in the customer's own words and ends with one clear, gentle action.

o2.biggest_strength: Shifts the mix decisively to sleep plus narrator clips, uses the exact customer phrases as hooks, and adds a genuinely fresh 'Lights down' live stream idea with a clear gate.
o2.biggest_mistake: The review logic is slightly loose ('no post names a condition, so none needs review') and one draft's 'Awake at 2am' title would in fact trip review rules, so the review plan needs tightening.

reason: Both are strong and on-brief; Output 2 wins on brand voice and originality, with stronger use of the customer's own words and a bolder, well-gated live-stream idea, though its review note needs one fix.
